clue.text: Writer's upset that cleric's upset about end of narrative arc

indicators.note: the jumbled clerical letters go around the turned-over writer's words
the second upset tells us to throw the letters of the cleric's word into disorder
in a down clue, being upset turns the writer's words upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: the writer of a clue speaks of themself as I, so 'writer is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the word narrative

explanation.surface: An author is put out because a churchman is annoyed by how a story's arc ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I'M into MI; 'upset' again jumbles CLERICS into SECIRCL, which goes 'about' MI to give SEMICIRCL; 'end of' adds the E of narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircle is a particular kind of curve, so an arc is a broader term covering it.

clue.text: Return sweater and blouse, finally, to French Connection

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of sweater and of blouse

parts.note: the thread linking the theme answers (LIME, OLIVE, BOTTLE, EMERALD, TURTLE) is green, and the French word for green is vert

explanation.surface: A shopper takes a jumper and a blouse back to the French Connection clothing store.
explanation.walkthrough: French Connection is a British fashion chain, but here it means the French for the puzzle's connecting theme, green. 'and' and 'to' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to go back to an earlier state, a synonym of the verb return.

clue.text: Quantities served in pubs and bars

definitions.meaning: spirits in British pubs are poured in fixed amounts, single or double tots
in music a bar is one of the units into which a score is divided

explanation.surface: Drinks dished up across pubs and bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: tots of spirit poured in pubs, and the American musical term for bars.

clue.text: Sailor posted miles away

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
a posted letter has been sent

explanation.surface: A seaman is stationed somewhere far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miles away' looks like distance, but means daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone miles away is lost in thought, which is the absent-minded sense of the word.

clue.text: Part of hose man used to support raised beds

indicators.note: in a down clue the chess man sits beneath the raised beds, holding them up
raised in a down clue means the word for the beds is read from the bottom up

parts.note: cots are small beds
the king is a piece, or man, in chess

explanation.surface: A gardener uses a length of hosepipe to prop up raised flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests a garden hose; it is old-fashioned legwear, and raised beds suggests gardening rather than COTS turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is a collective word for legwear, of which a single leg covering is one item.

clue.text: Obscure second book is excluded from marketing material

indicators.note: the book letter is left out of the promotional word

parts.note: a blurb is the promotional text on a book jacket
B is the abbreviation for book; here it is the second of the two in the promotional word

explanation.surface: An obscure sequel is left out of the publisher's promotional push.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to make it indistinct, which is the verb sense of smudge or fog.

clue.text: Religious figure continually pursuing right to die

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the word for continually comes after the right letter

parts.note: ever means always, continually
to end is to die, to come to a finish

explanation.surface: A clergyman is constantly pressing for the right to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title and term for a member of the clergy, a religious figure.

clue.text: Feeling tired and thirsty having wrapped stool up

indicators.note: the thirsty word wraps round the turned-up stool

parts.note: dry means thirsty

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: stool is the medical word for faeces, and poo is the informal one

explanation.surface: Someone tired and parched who has bundled up a stool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stool' looks like furniture but is the medical word for faeces; 'up' is the reversal signal in a down clue, and 'having wrapped' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy describes someone sagging and listless, which is how being worn out feels.

clue.text: Vessel ran short with too much on board

indicators.note: on board means inside, carried within the cut-down word
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a dye that ran bled
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A ship ran low on supplies even though it had too much loaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'on board' suggest a ship; the vessel holds liquid. 'short' cuts BLED to BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any container for liquid, and a glass flask for wine is one.

clue.text: Fiction about money being something that grows on trees

indicators.note: the untruth goes around the money letter

parts.note: a lie is an untruth, a fiction
M is the abbreviation for money, as in economics

explanation.surface: The story that money grows on trees is a fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the saying that money does not grow on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit is produced on trees, so it is literally something growing on them.

clue.text: What's extracted from quarry pit?

definitions.meaning: a quarry is dug to get rock out of it
a pit is the hard seed in a fruit such as a cherry

explanation.surface: What gets dug out of a quarry pit?
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is what quarries yield, and the same word names the hard kernel of a plum or cherry.

clue.text: Issue warning to clubs using right to block promotion

indicators.note: the right letter blocks the promotion by sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A football authority warns clubs over using rights to block promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a referee warns a player by showing a yellow card, so 'card' is a verb meaning caution.
explanation.definitionFit: In football to book a player by holding up a yellow is to formally caution them.

clue.text: Season with Italian club

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club, usually just called Inter

explanation.surface: A footballer spends a season at an Italian club.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest of the four seasons of the year is the one meant.

clue.text: Fighter boxing first for title, money and action, of course

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the fighter's word goes around what follows

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

indicators.note: first for picks the opening letter of the word title

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A boxer fights first for a title, then for money and action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on a golf course, where this is the short-range stroke on the green. 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the gentle stroke rolling the ball into the hole is the action described.

clue.text: Amiable nature perhaps characteristic of hen parties round Tyneside?

indicators.note: the made-up word for having no gents goes round the North East letters

parts.note: a hen party is a women-only celebration before a wedding, so it is, jokingly, without gents
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: Is a kindly temperament typical of hen parties held around Newcastle?
explanation.walkthrough: The invented 'gentless' (lacking gents) is the joke the question mark flags. A hen party is the British bride-to-be's night out with female friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness and mildness of temperament are what an amiable nature consists of, so it is an example.

clue.text: It's said to put a smile on your face

definitions.text: It's said to put a smile on your face

parts.words: It's said to put a smile on your face
parts.note: photographers ask people to say a dairy word whose long vowel pulls the mouth into a grin

explanation.definitionFit: Saying this dairy food word before a photograph is the standard trick to make the face smile.

clue.text: Flue lining damaged flue filled with stuff

indicators.note: the duct word lines, sitting inside, the jumbled letters
damaged means the letters of the second flue are knocked out of order

parts.note: a flue is a duct or vent for smoke

explanation.surface: A chimney lining is damaged, so the flue is clogged with stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' is the anagram signal and 'lining' the container: the duct word sits inside the jumble. 'stuff' means happenings, not material.
explanation.definitionFit: A day packed with happenings is lively and busy, so plenty of stuff fills it.

clue.text: Fierce female academic limits students' fun

indicators.note: limits means bounds, so the academic encloses the student fun

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
rag is the annual round of student stunts held for charity in British universities

explanation.surface: A fierce woman lecturer curbs the students' fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British university tradition of charity fundraising pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering, formidable woman is informally described this way, after the fire-breathing beast.

clue.text: Try to bring up taking on shortened lease to reduce expenditure

indicators.note: the vomiting word takes on, holds inside, the trimmed lease word

parts.note: to retch is to try to vomit

indicators.note: shortened cuts off the final letter

parts.note: to rent is to lease

explanation.surface: A tenant tries to raise the subject of a short lease to cut costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting back spending is the economy sense of this word, as when companies make savings.

clue.text: Publicity about university grants

indicators.note: the publicity word goes about the university

parts.note: ads are advertisements, publicity
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a university

explanation.surface: Publicity about university grants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grants' looks like a noun for funding; it is the verb meaning concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to concede or acknowledge it, which is a synonym here.

clue.text: Mere lad turned out for expensive 11

indicators.note: turned out means rearranged, so the letters of mere lad are reordered

explanation.surface: A mere boy turned out to be a costly rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is STONE, so 'expensive 11' is a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A green gem of high value is a precious example of the rock at 11.

clue.text: Highly esteemed left-wing supporter of American party

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter is placed below the other letters

parts.note: a do is a party
red is the colour of the left in politics

explanation.surface: A left-wing backer of an American political party is highly regarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political; it is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loved and revered is what highly esteemed amounts to, a past participle in both.

clue.text: One shelled by time bomb releasing hydrogen

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of the hydrogen letter

parts.note: to bomb along is to hurtle, travel very fast
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Someone shelled by a time bomb that released hydrogen gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' suggests bombardment; it means having a shell. 'bomb' is the verb meaning speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea reptile carries its home on its back, so it is a creature with a shell.

clue.text: Change one's mind about name being included in lease

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the name letter is included inside the lease word

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: A landlord reconsiders over a name on a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and give in, abandoning a harsh decision previously taken.

clue.text: Gamble about third place in relay race

indicators.note: the gamble word goes about the picked letter

parts.note: to bet is to gamble

indicators.note: third place in picks the third letter of relay

explanation.surface: A punter bets on a team taking third place in the relay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to belt along.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt somewhere is informal for moving very fast, a synonym of the verb to race.

clue.text: Kind of dash used for some cycle lanes

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cyclists dash along some cycle lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like speed or a punctuation mark; it is panache.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of stylish flair or verve is a synonym of this borrowed French word.

clue.text: Woman ignoring man's resistance

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the resistance letter

parts.note: Oliver is a man's name
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A woman takes no notice of a man's opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, so any woman so called fits the clue.

clue.text: Arrangement prior to uptake of drugs policy

definitions.text: Arrangement prior to uptake of drugs
definitions.meaning: cocaine is laid out in a narrow strip before it is snorted

explanation.surface: An arrangement made before the adoption of a drugs policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of coke laid out for snorting, and the official position as in toeing the party one.

clue.text: What's produced by horse eating a couple of nuts?

definitions.text: What's produced by horse eating a couple of nuts?

indicators.note: eating means the horse word takes the picked letters inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: a couple of takes the first two letters of the word nuts

explanation.surface: What does a horse produce after eating a couple of nuts?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a fair description of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Dung from horses is the classic farmyard fertiliser, what a horse leaves behind.

clue.text: Complaint of Labour leader lacking in fluency

indicators.note: lacking in means the leader's letter is missing from the fluency word

parts.note: slickness is smooth fluency, as of a salesman's patter

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Labour leader lacks fluency in speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests a grievance; it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment, so illness is a synonym.
